_comment: Opportunity-Decay config. A lead is not a fact, it's a LIFECYCLE: it strengthens, weakens, resolves, or expires. Everything else in MonitorCLT *detects* opportunity; this is the only piece that *retires* it -- so a parcel that scored 80 on a tax delinquency that's since been paid, or one that sold last month, stops sitting at 80 forever. Three mechanisms: (1) RESOLUTION -- a resolving event cancels the matching open signal (tax paid, lien released, code case closed, or a sale that resolves the whole parcel). (2) DECAY -- a signal's weight halves every half_life_days, so a 2-week-old code case outweighs a 2-year-old one. (3) EXPIRY -- a signal with no refresh in expire_after_days is stale and drops out. Resolution and expiry remove a signal from 'active'; decay just scales it. Tune freely.
_wildcard_note: '*' resolvers fire against ANY open signal on the parcel: a sale/transfer/under-contract means the opportunity is gone or has moved to a new owner -- the lead is stale regardless of what distress was open.
